pitch.text: Meet Ordo, the A.I. maintenance engineer for your codebase, built on I.B.M. watson x dot A.I.

Technical debt grows quietly. It piles up unseen, until it becomes an outage, slow delivery, or a security incident. Today's scanners produce long, noisy reports, ranked by rule severity, with no business context and no fix path. So the list gets ignored.
Ordo closes that gap in one pass. It analyzes a GitHub repository, ranks every finding by real risk, turns the list into a roadmap, and prepares the fix, the tests, and the pull request.
The ranking is done by I.B.M. Granite on watson x dot A.I. Every finding gets an urgency, business impact, and fix effort score, plus a plain English reason. Let's see it live.

demo.text: This is Ordo's web app, running on Vercel. We'll scan a real project, Agora, straight from GitHub.
I click Scan Repo Now and paste the repository link. While Bob streams the scan, Ordo reads the code through the GitHub A.P.I. and runs five debt detectors.
Seconds later, the dashboard. Twenty findings, nineteen of them high urgency, each scored by the Granite model for urgency, impact, and effort, with its reasoning attached.
The overview breaks the debt down by category, shows repository stats, including zero test files, and lists the top issues.
The roadmap is written by the model too. An overall assessment, then three phases the team can schedule.
Open any issue to drill in. Ask why it is ranked here, and watson x explains its reasoning in plain English.
Then generate the fix. Ordo returns a step by step remediation plan, code hints, a testing strategy, and a pull request summary, ready to copy straight into GitHub with one click.

The same engine runs inside I.B.M. Bob, I.B.M.'s A.I. coding assistant. Ordo ships as a custom Bob mode with three skills, analyze repo, explain issue, and generate fix, so developers can do all of this from chat.
And the full pitch deck is one click away, under Docs.

close.text: Ordo turns software chaos into order. Try it today at ordo with bob dot vercel dot app.
